product.title: Front Office Challenge
product.summary: Run a sports agency live across three sessions, absorbing two surprises the facilitator controls.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students run an agency advising real players. In session one they split a payment across cash now, a safety net, future growth and a community promise, then a large payment arrives thirty days late while the bills still land, and they choose a recovery route. Session two builds a business: pick a sponsorship, design a camp, build an operating budget and close a funding gap. Session three raises money at an investor table, absorbs a supply-cost shock before opening week, and ends in a scored championship report.

delivery.devices: one shared device per agency, plus a facilitator device

facilitation.prep: The founder creates the class, reads out one short code, and controls all seven phases and both surprise reveals from a dashboard.

product.technology: React + Vite single-page app, Vercel serverless functions, Supabase Postgres

studentDataProfile.notes: Stores a self-chosen agency name, decisions, progress, feedback answers, a salted PIN hash and a hashed access token. The operating model document states that no email, legal name, password, IP-linked identity or click trail is stored. Row-level security is forced with no policies, so access is service-role only. Descriptive only.

governance.maturityBasis: 309 unit tests and twelve browser tests pass under a five-job CI pipeline, and the founder dashboard is genuinely built. It stops short of TESTED because the repo states plainly that no real student has used this build.

health.technicalBasis: Deploy configuration is complete but neither Supabase migration has been applied to a real project, so the live path has never run.
knownBlockers: Neither database migration has been applied to a real project — the first real deploy is still ahead.
Internal manifest and implementation docs are stale, still describing a pre-production state the code has long passed.
The master prompt specifies a different framework and session count than what shipped.

validation.notes: The QA log states 'No real student has used this build,' and the kid playtest plan is marked not yet run.

governance.notes: Founder-dependent by design — the whole product assumes one person driving phases live. That is a legitimate R&D posture, but it means no other instructor can currently run it.

provenance.evidence: README.md: 'A founder-led live online classroom simulation for grades 5–6.' simulation-manifest.json: audience 'grades-5-6', three sessions of 45 minutes. shared/classroom.ts defines 35 steps across seven server-gated phases. SESSION1_QA_LOG.md: 'No real student has used this build.'
openQuestions: The current build ships three sessions; the master prompt still specifies two. The shipped product is authoritative, but the discrepancy is unresolved in the repo.
